(p-٦٢٩٢)

(p-٦٢٩٣)

Al-Shihab said: This is a famous and subtle metaphor (isti'arah), like the metaphor of the firewood of Hell for sins.

And that his wealth and his deeds will not avail him anything, and he will burn as he will burn. We ask Allah for well-being.

He said: 'Then I am a warner to you before a severe punishment.' Abu Lahab said: 'Perish you for the whole day! Is it for this that you gathered us?' Then this surah was revealed."

Imam Ahmad narrated from Rabi'ah ibn Abbad al-Dili, who said: "I saw the Prophet (ﷺ) in the Jahiliyyah (pre-Islamic period) in the market of Dhu al-Majaz, saying: 'O people! Say: There is no god but Allah, and you will prosper,' while the people gathered around him. Behind him was a man with a handsome, fair face, squint-eyed, with two locks of hair, saying: 'He is a lying apostate.' He followed him wherever he went. I asked about him, and they said: 'This is his uncle, Abu Lahab.'" In another narration of his: "He follows him from behind, saying: 'O sons of so-and-so! This man wants you to abandon al-Lat and al-Uzza and your allies among the jinn, and to adopt what he has brought of innovation and misguidance. So do not listen to him, and do not follow him.'"

﴿His wealth will not avail him, nor what he earned.﴾ That is: what benefit did his wealth and what he earned bring him, from the anger of Allah upon him and his loss? So "what he earned" is his deeds, which he thought would be of some benefit to him. It has also been said that it refers to his children, because wealth and children are often paired together in many verses, and the Arabs used to prepare their children for calamities just as they did their wealth. So He denied that they would benefit him when the destruction (tibab) befell him.

(p-٦٢٩٢)

Al-Shihab (al-Khafaji) said: What the people of narration (ahl al-athar) have confirmed is that his sons, may Allah curse him, were three: Mutatib and Utbah, both of whom embraced Islam, and Utaybah (diminutive form). This is the one who called upon the Prophet (ﷺ) when he openly harmed him and displayed enmity toward him, and he returned his daughter and divorced her. The Prophet (ﷺ), may the blessings and peace of Allah be upon him, said: "O Allah, set a dog from Your dogs upon him." So a lion devoured him during a journey he undertook to Syria. Hassan, may Allah be pleased with him, said about this:

"Whoever returns this year to his family, the lion's prey is not one who returns."

He then said: It is said that Lahab is one of these (sons). Al-Tha'alabi said: From this it is known that the lion is called "dog" (kalb). And since it was attributed to Allah, it was the greatest of its kind.

﴿He will burn in a Fire of blazing flame.﴾ That is, of intense heat and kindling. It is the Fire of the Hereafter, as recompense for what he used to do of opposing the truth and striving against it.

﴿And his wife, the carrier of firewood.﴾ That is, his wife will also burn in it along with him. So "his wife" is marfu' (in the nominative case) either by way of 'atf (conjunction) upon the pronoun in "will burn," or as a mubtada' (subject), with "on her neck" being the khabar (predicate). It was read as ﴿ḥammalata﴾ in the accusative as a shatm (vituperation) and dhamm (blame), and in the nominative as na't (adjective), or badal (apposition), or 'atf bayan (explicative appositive). She was called this only because she used to gather words (yahtibu al-kalam) like firewood, and walk about spreading slander (namimah), as Mujahid, Ikrimah and Qatadah said.

Al-Zamakhshari said: It is said of one who goes about with tale-bearing, one who sows corruption among people, that he carries firewood among them, that is, he kindles (fire) among them and produces evil. He said:

"The fair ones were not caught upon the back of a coat of mail, nor did they walk among the tribe with green firewood."

He praises them as being of white (pure) faces, free from being caught in evil and baseness, and free from walking about with intrigue and slander among people. He made it "green" (ratb) to indicate smoke (tadkhin), which is an increase of evil. It is said: "So-and-so carries firewood against so-and-so," meaning he incites against him.

(p-٦٢٩٣)

Al-Shihab said: This is a famous and subtle metaphor (isti'arah), like the metaphor of the firewood of Hell for sins.

Ibn Kathir said: His wife was among the noblewomen of the Quraysh. She was Umm Jamil, and her name was Arwa bint Harb ibn Umayyah. She was the sister of Abu Sufyan and the aunt of Mu'awiyah, and she was a helper to her husband in his disbelief, obstinacy and stubbornness.

﴿On her neck a rope of palm fiber.﴾ The Imam, may Allah have mercy on him, said: That is, on her neck is a rope of fiber. That is, she has burdened herself with a grievous hardship, in order to cause corruption among people and to kindle the fires of enmity among them, like the carrier of firewood who has a coarse rope on his neck with which he binds what he has carried upon his neck, so that he can bear it. This is the most hideous image in which a woman carrying firewood may appear, with a rope of fiber on her neck, binding the firewood to her shoulder until she nearly chokes on it.

He also said: Allah has revealed this surah concerning Abu Lahab and this wife of his, so that it would be an example from which whoever opposes what Allah has sent down to His Prophet might take heed, by complying with his own desires and preferring what he has become accustomed to of beliefs, customs and actions, deceived by what he has of wealth, and by the authority or status he holds in the hearts of men. And that his wealth and his deeds will not avail him anything, and he will burn as he will burn. We ask Allah for well-being.

(p-٦٢٨٩)

In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.

Surah al-Masad

It is also called Surah Abi Lahab. It is Meccan, and its verses number five.

(p-٦٢٩٠)

In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.

On the interpretation of His saying, exalted is He:

[1–5] ﴿Perish the hands of Abu Lahab, and perish he. His wealth will not avail him, nor what he earned. He will burn in a Fire of blazing flame, and his wife, the carrier of firewood, will be on his neck a rope of palm fiber.﴾

﴿Perish the hands of Abu Lahab, and perish he.﴾ That is, his hands were lost, and he himself was lost. "The two hands" is a kinayah (metonymy) for the self and the person, because of the general connection between them, or it is a majaz (figurative usage) by way of mentioning a part to mean the whole. The clause "and perish he" is a ta'kid (emphasis) of what precedes it, or what is meant by the first is his loss in his own self and essence, because a person's striving is for the correction of his self and his deeds. So He informs that he is deprived of both, as the two verses after it indicate: namely, the ruin of his deeds and the ruin of his self.

Ibn Jarir said: Some of the people of Arabic grammar used to say that His saying ﴿Perish the hands of Abu Lahab﴾ is a supplication against him from Allah. As for His saying "and perish he," it is a statement of news, that is, about what will be realized for him in this world and the Hereafter. He expressed it in the past tense because of its certainty.

Abu Lahab was one of the paternal uncles of the Prophet (ﷺ). His name was Abd al-Uzza. He became well known by his kunyah (honorific nickname) and was recognized by it, either because of a son of his named Lahab, or because of the blazing (talahhub) and brightness of his cheeks, with an indication that he is among the people of the Fire and that his final destination is a fire of blazing flame. His condition thus matched his kunyah, so mentioning him by it was fitting.

(p-٦٢٩١)
